data.title: bn-27k: M1.5.2.3 Cleanup only what the run created

data.body: HIGH — Deletion authority can be granted by a non-creation response. Any 2xx with an ID is accepted, including 202 Accepted or 200 returning an existing object. The registered fixture reports actual creation with 201. In a relogin retry, complete_body also falls back to a complete earlier request if the terminal retry body is incomplete, pairing the retry status with a different response's ID. Require the registered proof of creation and the exact terminal flow that produced it, or keep the object owed without deletion. The same-name fixture always returns a newly allocated ID and never exercises either case.

HIGH — Both per-object intent rows receive the identical digest of the entire two-action batch. Their individual requests are never hashed, and the role is skipped by serialization. A crash after sending one removal leaves both rows owed, with the same intent and no durable indication of which action crossed the dispatch boundary. Persist a distinct exact per-object request binding and dispatch boundary before each removal. Verify the first and second crash boundaries independently.

HIGH — A single cleanup error classifies every eligible object Unknown if the shared step exists. Losing the first response leaves the second deletion unattempted, but its record falsely claims an attempted unknown effect. Losing the second response also replaces the first confirmed outcome with Unknown and drops the first action's acquired flows from the returned round. The existing lost-response test explicitly expects both Unknown after exactly one send. Persist and retain each observed outcome, separate the in-flight object from remaining obligations, and preserve prior receipts.

HIGH — Failure reading the cleanup flow floor occurs before the RunStep exists. cleanup_objects intentionally returns success with the objects Owed and cleanup_step set. link_originals then unconditionally requires that missing RunStep and returns CaptureMismatch. The public entry point discards the acquired round even though the observations and capture succeeded. Link only actual cleanup flows and cover this case through finalization.

HIGH — The schema accepts Complete without any effect, receipt or flows and also Complete with a not-sent receipt and Effect::None. Independently confirmed both inserts after upgrading a populated v10 database. record_cleanup permits an initial terminal row, and a Failed/None row can transition to Complete/None under the public transition rules; cleanup_summary then clears the obligation. Enforce coherent effect/outcome/receipt combinations on initial writes and updates, and prevent Unknown evidence from being cleared to NULL.

HIGH — Every 2xx removal is recorded Complete, including 202 Accepted, which only acknowledges queued work. That can clear the final cleanup obligation while the object still exists. Classify the registered removal's terminal success distinctly from accepted or otherwise inconclusive responses. The registered fixture's completed deletion returns 204.

MEDIUM — AcquiredRound.cleanup is copied before finalization links original artifacts in the store. ExecutedRounds returns that earlier copy unchanged, so even a successful cleanup has null original references in the public result while recover_cleanup returns linked originals. The success test only inspects the reloaded store. Populate the returned records after linking and compare public results to the recovered records.

MEDIUM — The cancel/expiry test injects a NotSent receipt directly. The live send adapter never produces this receipt on refusal: sent_request rejects empty hop lists and native error envelopes return InvocationError, which the cleanup batch converts to Unknown for every object. The test cannot establish the claimed exact failed/no-effect outcome on this production path. Check a known pre-dispatch refusal through the native adapter separately from an ambiguous transport loss and preserve the distinction in durable cleanup.

MEDIUM — The requested zero-DELETE case is tested only when the first plant reply is lost. If the second reply is lost, primary_id remains set and cleanup_objects dispatches one DELETE before acquisition returns the uncertainty. The primary has its own established receipt, so this is safe under a per-object interpretation of POR-11, but the run does not meet a blanket zero-DELETE requirement. Exercise loss at both positions and decide explicitly whether the entire round must abstain.

data.reason: Pinned 5d52c2919886d528800f40019ad35a1a88c4e619 grants deletion authority from non-creation responses, conflates independent cleanup attempts and outcomes, loses completed observations on a pre-dispatch failure, and can mark an unresolved deletion complete. Six high and three medium threads document the affected paths.

data.body: Fixed in 4f513ba: cleanup now abstains for the whole round when either plant response is uncertain; the established sibling remains Owed, and both first-loss and second-loss zero-DELETE cases are covered.

Fixed in 4f513ba: execute_live refreshes every AcquiredRound cleanup record from the store after finalization/linking, and the success regression compares public cleanup records with recover_cleanup including exact originals.

Fixed in 4f513ba: ownership requires Effect::Observed, exact status 201, a valid ID from the exact terminal complete request/retry flow; 200 existing, 202 accepted, and incomplete terminal retry regressions retain no deletion authority.

Fixed in 4f513ba: C retains the frozen batch RunStep while each object binds a distinct one-action digest and commits its own InFlight record before dispatch; independent first/second crash boundaries are tested.

Fixed in 4f513ba: cleanup failures transition only the current object; an unattempted sibling remains Owed, completed prior receipts/flows remain Complete, and both lost-response positions assert exact per-object outcomes and send counts.
Fixed in 4f513ba: Complete now requires an observed 204 plus an exact terminal complete request/retry flow; 202 and incomplete 204 remain Unknown with regressions.

Fixed in 4f513ba: a passive flow-floor failure before the RunStep leaves both obligations Owed, linking skips cleanup rows with no flows, and the finalization regression preserves the acquired round and all 11 original flows.

Fixed in 4f513ba: native exit-4 dependency refusals with stable cancel/pass-expiry reasons map through the production error path to Failed/Effect::None, while ambiguous transport loss remains Unknown; direct typed NotSent controls remain separate.

Fixed in 4f513ba: schema and record_cleanup coherence now require exact outcome/effect/status/flow combinations; recovery is monotone through InFlight, rejects impossible Complete and Failed-to-Complete changes, and never clears Unknown evidence.

data.reason: At 4f513ba the pinned native adapter can return exit 4 after dispatch, but cleanup records no effect. Independent SQLite and public Store probes admit impossible completion and reject a known-not-created settlement. Ambiguous duplicate ID fields still grant deletion authority.

data.body: HIGH, 4f513ba. 200/202 and a retained partial terminal retry now abstain. The 201 path still grants authority when the plant response contains two conflicting id members: rounds.rs:1486 parses into serde_json::Value and silently picks the last member. The independent parser probe confirmed the previously existing ID was selected from an ambiguous response. Require one unambiguous identifier before granting deletion authority. The new test covers a partial retained retry only.

HIGH, 4f513ba. rounds.rs:1394 treats every native exit 4 with a reason as proof of zero effect. In the pinned Teapot 6238d5a78, crates/teapot-engine/src/commands/requests.rs:340-396 explicitly returns exit 4 and the stop reason when a request already written is interrupted. replay/send.rs:583-607 records its sent bytes. Identical exit/reason can mean pre-dispatch refusal or in-flight interruption. Readback errors also enter this classifier after an observed dispatch; attempting to overwrite the existing reference/status can return Store::Conflict and discard the round. The new test synthesizes the diagnostic and never establishes its timing. Preserve uncertainty when the native evidence cannot distinguish these cases.

HIGH, 4f513ba. Independent v10->11 SQLite probes accepted Complete with an absent effect or absent response status because SQL CHECK passes NULL. Observed InFlight/Unknown without a receipt and Failed/None with status 204 also pass. An external Rust caller linked against this exact commit recorded Observed/InFlight without a reference, changed Observed to None while InFlight, and recorded Complete with a not-sent reference, a sibling object's retained flow and a missing terminal retry. All writes succeeded. The public validator filters out missing terminal flow IDs and accepts any prefix and reference. Validate coherent rows and evidence-preserving transitions at both boundaries; a valid 204 control passed and a 202 completion was rejected.

HIGH — On 4f513ba the ownership transition allows Pending to NotCreated but the outcome transition forbids Owed to NotRequired. This is the exact combination plant_object submits when it receives definitive no-effect evidence. An external caller linked against the pinned commit reproduced StoreError::Conflict; the original Pending/Owed record survives and a fully known non-creation cannot be reconciled. Exercise the real public transition along with conservative unknown cases.

The exact original already carries HTTP status, but rounds.rs:536 drops it when constructing Readback. Only method/URL are compared at :1222. A retained original whose status contradicts the send receipt can therefore still supply the deletion ID. The same applies to evidence of a completed removal. Reject contradictions between the terminal original and its receipt.

data.reason: Verified at 4f513ba. Both absent plant positions now abstain; first- and second-loss cleanup tests passed against the pinned archive.
Verified at 4f513ba. The one-action digest is committed for each object; begin_cleanup_action commits its individual in-flight boundary before dispatch. The original frozen batch step remains.
Verified at 4f513ba. The first-loss and second-loss regressions agree with per-object dispatch order and durable outcomes, including first-object flow preservation after second-object loss.

Verified at 4f513ba. The normal removal receipt path now leaves 202 and partial terminal 204 unresolved; the 202-specific false completion is fixed. Remaining contradictory-evidence storage cases are tracked separately.
Verified at 4f513ba. Pre-dispatch passive floor failure leaves both objects owed, linking skips rows without flows, and the focused finalization test passes.
Verified at 4f513ba. The public execution path refreshes each round's cleanup records after immutable originals have been linked.

data.body: Fixed in 81aacd5: plant IDs now deserialize through a duplicate-key-rejecting typed struct; terminal retained original status is carried only inside acquisition and must exactly equal the dispatch receipt for both 201 creation and 204 removal. Conflicting duplicate IDs and plant/cleanup receipt-original status mismatches now abstain with zero inferred authority/completion.

Fixed in 81aacd5: native exit/reason errors are always Unknown because pinned Teapot can emit exit 4 after sending; only an actual typed DispatchEvidence::NotSent receipt records Failed/Effect::None. Native pass-expired/cancel-requested and typed NotSent cases are separate regressions.

Fixed in 81aacd5: SQL uses COALESCE-safe terminal constraints, observed requires an exact flow reference, Complete binds exact object prefix/terminal complete flow/reference/status, Failed/None forbids status, and the monotonic trigger freezes identity/evidence while permitting only exact null-original enrichment. Rust mirrors these rules and forbids InFlight downgrade. Direct public and raw-SQL probes cover NULL effect/status, not-sent/sibling/missing-terminal Complete, observed-without-reference, evidence downgrade, row moves, flow rewrite/deletion/reorder/substitution, plus valid enrichment.

Fixed in 81aacd5: Owed now transitions to NotRequired only with the coherent Pending-to-NotCreated settlement; the public store regression proves the exact transition while conservative Unknown states remain unresolved.

data.reason: At 81aacd5e, the plant ID parser accepts a one-element array without the registered /id field and can grant deletion authority. The public store can attach an original that disagrees with the same committed RunStep, and SQL still accepts incoherent receipts and malformed original enrichment.

data.body: HIGH at 81aacd5e. Duplicate member and original-status disagreement now abstain, but the new derived ObjectIdReply also accepts a positional JSON array. An independent Rust probe using the exact struct definition decoded a one-element array as the ID despite the registered /id member being absent. The positive object control passed and duplicate id members were rejected. Require the top-level map shape and exactly one id member before an observed 201 grants authority.

HIGH at 81aacd5e. The original null-status/effect and reference mismatch cases now reject. Fresh raw SQLite probes still accepted (1) an in-flight unknown effect rewritten to NULL through the trigger at line 77, (2) failed/not-sent/effect-none with status 500 at line 46, (3) an initial Complete evidence list containing a sibling object's earlier flow and a valid terminal flow at line 39, and (4) null-original enrichment to a non-digest string at line 101, making typed recovery fail. Changing/removing an already linked original, reordering existing flows, switching a prior flow's object, and moving the row were rejected; well-formed enrichment succeeded. Exercise normal inserts and updates as well as the exact NULL branches.

HIGH at 81aacd5e. link_cleanup_originals accepts a different, well-formed artifact than the original already durably linked to its C RunStep. An external caller recorded flow 77 with original a1 in the step, supplied b1 as the cleanup enrichment for that same flow, and received Ok(11). Independent readback confirmed run_steps=77/a1 and run_cleanup=77/b1. The production linking sequence already writes the RunStep first; compare cleanup enrichments against that exact run/step/flow binding before accepting them. Guard the raw enrichment path consistently if it is part of the store contract.

data.reason: Verified at 81aacd5e: native exit 4 with a stop/expiry reason preserves unknown effects, and only the explicit NotSent receipt records a definitive failed/no-effect cleanup.
Verified at 81aacd5e with an external caller: Pending/Owed to NotCreated/NotRequired succeeded, and recoverable cleanup reports NotRequired.

data.body: Fixed in 4eb95c6: ObjectIdReply now uses the shared map-only deserializer plus duplicate-key-rejecting canonical input, so a root array, duplicate id, extra member, or missing /id cannot establish ownership; the exact positional-array regression now abstains.

Fixed in 4eb95c6: COALESCE-safe monotonic SQL rejects Unknown-to-NULL; Failed/None requires NULL status; INSERT/UPDATE triggers validate every flow's exact object prefix, shape, typed fields, artifact ID and 64-lowercase-hex digest, and require exact binding to the already-durable C RunStep. Raw probes cover initial sibling flow, malformed enrichment, no-effect 500, NULL downgrade, cleanup-before-step, and valid exact enrichment.

Fixed in 4eb95c6: each C action's flows are appended to the frozen RunStep before its terminal per-object cleanup write. link_cleanup_originals now loads cleanup_step and requires every enriched flow/artifact to equal a committed step flow; SQL INSERT/UPDATE triggers enforce the same binding. Public and raw mismatched-artifact probes reject while exact enrichment succeeds.

data.reason: At exact target 4eb95c61, the public store and SQLite accept Complete after dropping the C step’s missing terminal retry or borrowing another round’s C step. The new shared prefix rule also lets record_step append an artifact-bearing flow after a settled, unrelated step.

data.body: HIGH at 4eb95c61: mismatched original now rejects and matching enrichment succeeds. The new binding checks membership, not the exact ordered flow list for this round and object. Both a separately compiled public Store caller and independent raw SQL recorded Complete by omitting the C step’s missing terminal retry and reporting only its earlier retained request. Both also accepted round 2’s cleanup bound to round 1’s C step. Compare against the complete ordered per-object projection from the correct round C step (including duplicates, missing entries and terminal position) on initial writes, updates and linking.

HIGH — The new prefix-growth rule is applied to every step, including settled non-cleanup steps. The public API accepted appending an additional flow that already carried an original to a nonempty I1 step with Effect::Observed; the previous nonempty receipt rule rejected this change. Existing-flow rewrites still reject, so the current regression test misses the append behavior. Limit incremental append to the still-open C action boundaries that require it, freeze settled receipts, and require newly appended acquired flows to await the ordinary original-link path.

data.reason: Verified at 4eb95c61: map-only input, duplicate-member checking and terminal status consistency reject the prior false-authority examples. The registered fixture returns the single declared id field.

Verified at 4eb95c61 on an immutable source archive: the pinned old NULL downgrade, nonexistent/incorrect reference, no-effect plus 500, sibling flow, malformed artifact, earlier original change and row move probes reject. Exact enrichment succeeds. The separate per-object flow-list binding issue is tracked on th-msks2c.

data.body: Fixed in 872f8ee: every cleanup write now binds cleanup_step to canonical round*12 and the exact round.<n>.C step, then requires the complete ordered per-object projection with positional tuple equality and equal projection length. Public record/update/link plus raw INSERT/UPDATE reject omitted retry, reordering/duplicates mismatch, and cross-round binding; exact full projection remains valid.

Fixed in 872f8ee: step flow growth is frozen once effects are settled; appended flows before settlement must preserve the exact existing prefix, carry original=None, and only a canonical nonempty round.<n>.C step may grow incrementally. Normal empty-to-acquired steps remain valid. Public probes reject settled appended flows with either linked or null originals, pending prelinked append, and a second append to an open non-C step; live C rounds remain green.

data.reason: At exact 872f8ee6 the public step writer can append a missing retry for a completed object and leave the object and run marked Complete. A terminal Failed cleanup with no batch step is also accepted. The new append guard prevents an Unknown step with no flows from settling with its first recovered receipt.

data.body: HIGH at 872f8ee6. A cleanup write now checks its ordered projection, correct round and step. The reverse write can immediately invalidate the accepted result: I recorded one primary flow, recorded primary Complete, correctly appended a control flow, then appended a missing primary retry to the still-open C step. Public record_step accepted both appends; recovery returned three step flows but only one primary cleanup flow and both primary/run Complete. Guard writes on the C-step side too, while retaining the valid subsequent control append. Separately, public and SQL inserts accepted a terminal Failed/not-sent row with no C RunStep because the list was empty (store/mod.rs:1641). Only pre-dispatch intent may precede that durable boundary, including when the eventual receipt has no retained flow.

MEDIUM at 872f8ee6. The previous append after a settled non-C step now rejects for both null and populated originals. The fix also prevents the legitimate transition from Unknown with zero flows to Observed with the first recovered matching, null-original flow. I compiled and ran equivalent external Store callers against both pinned trees: base a4228fbb accepted that transition, new 872f8ee6 returned Conflict. The existing unknown-settlement test supplies no recovered flow and misses this regression. Preserve the evidence-backed initial settlement while continuing to reject appends to conclusively settled receipts.

Fixed in ea37503: Rust and SQL now gate every new C flow on that object's durable boundary. Only InFlight or the exact flowless-Unknown recovery may grow; Complete/Failed/NotRequired cannot gain a late retry while an InFlight sibling still can. InFlight and terminal cleanup rows require the canonical round C RunStep, with only Owed allowed before it. Exact public/raw late-primary and missing-step probes pass.

Fixed in ea37503: the generic Store transition again accepts the exact base-compatible Unknown/zero-flow receipt with no instrument reference settling to Observed with one F0.request flow (id 77, null original). It remains limited to the first unlinked flow; settled nonempty/conclusive steps still cannot grow. The C variant additionally requires the exact flow-bound Unknown object and is covered through Complete.

HIGH at ea375036a391c977b2ce856bf2995dc0d67735ca, 011_run_cleanup.sql lines 127-137. Public record_step and a literal raw late append now reject. The SQL trigger trusts the old prefix and only inspects indices at or beyond its old length. I built a valid Primary Complete and Control InFlight via the public API, then updated the C sequence from [primary.request 77, control.request 78] to [primary.request 77, primary.retry 81, control.request 78]. SQLite accepted the late retry and still reports Primary Complete with only flow 77. Same-length replacement of 77 with 7, shrinking out the primary, and renaming the canonical C step also succeeded on a rollback-only database. Enforce the previously durable prefix, immutable canonical identity, and allowed enrichment on the step side, while retaining legitimate sibling append and original linking. The separate missing-C terminal and InFlight probes now reject correctly.

HIGH at ea375036a391c977b2ce856bf2995dc0d67735ca, store/mod.rs lines 1597-1608 and 1680-1697 and 011_run_cleanup.sql lines 150-158. The exact base-compatible generic first flow now succeeds and settled growth still rejects. However, the new recovery path requires an ID but never compares it to the durable pre-send floor. An independent public Store caller reproduced the exact Unknown/empty C record with reference flow:77, prior Observed action and status 204. Recovery accepted ID 77 with floors 77 and 78, then record_cleanup returned Complete in both cases. With floor 10 the positive control likewise completed; ID 88 against reference 77 rejected. The live execution guard in rounds.rs:1218 explicitly rejects IDs at or below the floor before readback. Enforce the same fresh-flow rule at new recovery evidence acceptance, including the per-object/step and direct SQL paths.

MEDIUM at ea375036a391c977b2ce856bf2995dc0d67735ca. An observed DELETE with a retained flow and no HTTP response status is classified as Failed, which the Store rejects for Observed unless a non-2xx status exists (store/mod.rs:2008-2015). The send parser accepts matching null outer/hop statuses and flow readback permits a null status. With the target classifier and a real public Store I reproduced Failed, Err(Conflict), with the durable object still InFlight. The error escapes cleanup_objects and execute_live drops the acquired rounds at execution?, contrary to F-27. Classify this ambiguous response as Unknown, or reject it before the terminal transition using the existing unknown-preserving path. Cover retained/no-status receipt plus matching status-less readback and verify that the acquired round and cleanup evidence survive. This is an adapter-contract case; no claim that the pinned binary naturally emitted it.

data.reason: BLOCK on ea375036a391c977b2ce856bf2995dc0d67735ca. Raw C-step updates can change the evidence behind a terminal object (th-msks2c). Unknown recovery can report Complete from a pre-send flow (th-2skrba). A retained cleanup flow without HTTP status triggers a Store conflict and loses the public round result (th-3jg9zt).

data.body: Fixed in 1f1bc76: a new raw-SQL run_steps monotonic trigger freezes run/number/name/digest/floor, preserves the exact old flow prefix, rejects shrink/replacement/insertion-before-tail, and permits only typed null-original append or exact original enrichment. The per-object C boundary remains layered on top. Raw late suffix, insertion before control, replacement, shrink, and C-step rename all reject; valid sibling growth and enrichment remain green.

Fixed in 1f1bc76: first-flow recovery now requires the retained ID to be strictly greater than the durable pre-send floor in generic Rust, per-object C Rust, generic SQL, and C SQL paths. Exact ID 77/floor 10 completes; floors 77 and 78 reject through both public Store and raw SQL and leave cleanup Unknown.

Fixed in 1f1bc76: an Observed cleanup receipt with no HTTP status is now Unknown, matching the Store contract instead of attempting an impossible Failed transition. An adapter-level retained-flow probe with matching null receipt/readback statuses proves the acquired round survives, originals link exactly, primary remains Unknown, sibling completes, and the run summary is Partial.

data.reason: Verified at 1f1bc765b3cebee1097e75599c5176996d6002f9. The prior independent observed/no-status classifier and Store probe returned Unknown and persisted it. The mock round with matching null receipt/readback kept the acquired round, linked the original, completed its sibling, and returned Partial.

data.body: HIGH at 1f1bc765b3cebee1097e75599c5176996d6002f9, store/011_run_cleanup.sql:123-136, 193-200 and 225-235. Regular UPDATE insertion before control, replacement of the primary ID, shrink, reorder, and rename now reject. Legal sibling append and well-formed original enrichment succeed. The same-length branch still accepts a two-key original {artifact_id,extra} with no digest or {extra,digest} with no artifact_id: the missing member yields SQL NULL inside NOT(...). I persisted the first shape in a disposable copy and reopened the public Store; recover_run returned Err(Decode) while recover_cleanup still returned Complete. Also reproduced a raw INSERT OR REPLACE of the existing canonical C row changing primary ID 77 to 7, and adding an unrecognized C.primary.other suffix after primary completion. Enforce exact enrichment with NULL-safe rejection and freeze the canonical C evidence across replacement and deletion as well as UPDATE, including allowed C tail labels.

HIGH at 1f1bc765b3cebee1097e75599c5176996d6002f9, store/mod.rs:1632-1634 and 1682-1684, store/011_run_cleanup.sql:248. The later flowless Unknown settlement now rejects id 77 at floors 77/78 and accepts it at floor 10 through public Store and SQL. The earlier real crash window remains open: execute_step commits InFlight/Observed, reference flow:77 and status 204 before its readback floor check in rounds.rs. I persisted that state with an empty pending C step, closed/reopened the Store, recorded recovered C.primary.request 77, then recorded the 204 terminal outcome. All three floors 10, 77 and 78 returned Ok(Complete); equivalent raw writes also completed. Enforce the durable floors for every newly retained ID, including acquisition/resume of an InFlight row. The raw generic Unknown branch additionally accepted id 77 at floor 10 with an existing instrument_reference flow:88, unlike public Rust; preserve the exact recovered-reference binding there too.

data.reason: BLOCK at 1f1bc765b3cebee1097e75599c5176996d6002f9. Reopening durable InFlight can certify stale evidence as Complete (th-2skrba). Raw SQL can corrupt, replace, or remove canonical step evidence and break public recovery (th-msks2c). Status-less receipt finding th-3jg9zt is resolved.

data.body: Fixed at 23a3e62: same-length original enrichment is now NULL-safe and requires the exact two-key Artifact shape with a present nonempty ID and lowercase 64-hex digest. put_step uses validated UPDATE for existing rows; a BEFORE INSERT duplicate guard blocks INSERT OR REPLACE, bound canonical C rows cannot be deleted, and both initial and appended C flows admit only the frozen primary/control request/redirect/login/retry labels and typed null originals. Direct raw probes reject both missing-member originals, REPLACE, DELETE, and C.primary.other; exact enrichment and legitimate sibling growth still pass.

Fixed at 23a3e62: every newly retained flow ID must be strictly greater than the durable RunStep floor, and canonical C growth additionally compares against that object's persisted cleanup floor for both InFlight and narrowly recoverable Unknown rows. The raw generic Unknown recovery path also requires its instrument_reference to be absent or equal the recovered flow. A close/reopen crash-window matrix accepts floor 10 but rejects public and raw ID 77 at floors 77/78 while leaving cleanup InFlight; the mismatched flow:88/raw-flow-77 probe also rejects.

data.reason: Verified at 23a3e62ab48db26c7d1436d4bba2a7a5087ec470. Independent public close/reopen and raw SQL probes accepted flow 77 at floor 10, rejected it at floors 77/78 for InFlight and Unknown, and separately rejected step/object floor disagreement when either floor was 77. Raw generic recovery rejected reference flow:88 for ID 77. Valid first unlinked generic recovery and adjacent frozen-receipt checks passed.

data.body: HIGH at 23a3e62ab48db26c7d1436d4bba2a7a5087ec470, 011_run_cleanup.sql:113-136 and 145-170. The previous missing nested artifact fields, canonical row REPLACE, DELETE, rename, and unregistered suffix now reject. Same-length enrichment still accepts replacing a required null top-level flow member (original or decoder) with an unrelated fifth key: JSON extraction sees both missing and JSON null as SQL NULL. I reproduced both on bundled rusqlite 0.43; after reopening, public recover_run returned Err(Decode) while recover_cleanup still reported Complete. The same write/read failure occurred with a digest of 64 hex chars followed by NUL plus one char, an unpaired surrogate in the artifact ID, and a newly appended sibling flow ID of 18446744073709551616. Positive controls for valid original enrichment and max-u64 ID both decoded. Require strict decodability of the full canonical flow and artifacts in each path, including required nullable member presence, decoded text and integer bounds.

HIGH at 23a3e62ab48db26c7d1436d4bba2a7a5087ec470. The per-object run_cleanup monotonic guard applies only to UPDATE. An ordinary INSERT OR REPLACE of an existing row bypassed its ownership/evidence transition and removed an outstanding obligation. On the bundled SQLite with foreign keys and recursive triggers enabled I started from an established object with an Unknown cleanup and flow:77, replaced its same-key row with NotCreated/NotRequired and no evidence, and reopened the public Store. Replaying that recovered row via record_cleanup returned Ok(NotRequired) and changed the run summary from Unknown to NotRequired. Preserve existing cleanup rows across replacement and deletion, including idempotent public updates and legitimate monotone settlements. This is a separate ledger from the now-protected canonical run_steps row.

data.reason: BLOCK on 23a3e62ab48db26c7d1436d4bba2a7a5087ec470. Bundled SQLite accepted undecodable canonical step evidence (th-msks2c) and replacement of an outstanding per-object cleanup with NotRequired (th-14rs67). The durable flow-floor and reference recovery finding th-2skrba is resolved.

data.body: Fixed at 5e68b9a: run_steps now validates the full frozen Flow shape on every INSERT and flow_refs UPDATE before monotonic checks. All five required parent keys must be present; required-nullable types stay explicit; text must be nonempty, NUL-free and SQLite/Rust-decodable; Artifact/VersionedId nested keys are exact; digest uses an exact quoted 64-lower-hex token; retained IDs use exact decimal syntax bounded through u64::MAX. Reopen probes reject swapped original/decoder keys, NUL-tailed digest, unpaired surrogate and u64::MAX+1, while valid enrichment and u64::MAX recover exactly.

Fixed at 5e68b9a: put_cleanup now uses a validated UPDATE for an existing per-object row and INSERT only for a new key. BEFORE INSERT and BEFORE DELETE guards prevent raw INSERT OR REPLACE and deletion from recreating or erasing the cleanup ledger. The exact established/Unknown flow:77 case now rejects replacement with NotCreated/NotRequired and deletion; after close/reopen the original Unknown record is byte-equivalent, idempotent public replay remains Unknown, and the run summary cannot be cleared.

HIGH, exact 5e68b9a418da85288fd0e070a655af6233f8ff2b. Prior missing fields, escaped surrogate, NUL-tailed digest and oversized integer reject; valid original and u64::MAX both reopen. The new shape guard still accepts a trailing comma on an otherwise identical flow array: bundled SQLite permits JSON5 in json_each/json_type. On run_steps the write returned Ok(1), then public recover_run returned Decode; the equivalent run_cleanup write made recover_cleanup return Decode. An invalid UTF-8 byte inside a raw TEXT artifact ID likewise passed, including SQLite json_valid=1, then the public reader returned Utf8Error. Also, the new validator accepts a valid VersionedId object, but the old branches at SQL lines 287, 374, 571, 673 still require text. Public Store rejected an ordinary pending step acquiring its first flow with decoder {id:http,version:1}; initial insertion with that typed decoder succeeded. Apply strict Rust-readable JSON/UTF-8 to both ledgers, and use the frozen VersionedId shape consistently on initial writes, append, and cleanup projection.

HIGH, exact 5e68b9a418da85288fd0e070a655af6233f8ff2b, 011_run_cleanup.sql:327, 337, 526, 538. Matching logical-key REPLACE, direct DELETE and backwards UPDATE now reject; reopen/public replay stays Unknown. Both tables also have a hidden rowid uniqueness constraint. With the bundled default recursive_triggers=0 (Store enables foreign keys and FULL sync only), a replacement using the existing primary rowid and a different logical role passed the duplicate-key INSERT guard, and SQLite silently removed the old row without its delete trigger firing. After reopen the sole cleanup was Control/NotRequired, and public replay changed the run summary from Unknown to NotRequired.
